nodes.description:
The hair bundle is an array of actin-cored stereocilia held at fixed, graded heights. Without class III myosin function the bundle is built wrongly: mice lacking both myosin IIIa and IIIb show abnormally tall and numerous microvilli or stereocilia, ungraded bundles, and bundle rounding and closure. The direction of that result is the opposite of what the espin-1 transport model predicts on its own - the motors act to limit elongation and to shape the bundle, not simply to lengthen it.
A single-gene Myo3a knock-in carrying a kinase-domain missense allele also shows structural abnormality of cochlear hair cell stereocilia, which is the closer model of the human recessive disease. Mechanoelectrical transduction currents themselves were robust with normal kinetics in the double mutants, so this is a bundle-architecture defect rather than a transduction-channel defect.

nodes.description:
Myosin IIIa is a plus-end-directed motor that accumulates at the tips of stereocilia, which is where the actin core is polymerised, and it carries cargo there - most clearly espin-1, an ankyrin-repeat espin isoform that binds actin monomers through a WH2 motif. Co-expressing myosin IIIa with espin-1 elongates filopodia about tenfold in COS-7 cells, and that elongation requires the transport step and the espin-1 WH2 activity, not merely the presence of both proteins.
Loss of the motor therefore removes a tip-localised regulator of actin dynamics. The cargo-delivery account is incomplete on its own: in mice lacking both class III myosins, espin-1 was still properly targeted to stereocilia tips, so myosin IIIa is not the only route for espin-1 and the phenotype cannot be reduced to failed espin-1 delivery.

nodes.description:
Biallelic loss-of-function variants remove or disable myosin IIIa. The founding family carried a nonsense allele truncating the C terminus of the motor head plus two splice alleles, and later families carry missense alleles in the motor and kinase domains. Myosin IIIa is a hybrid motor-signalling molecule: an N-terminal kinase domain that autophosphorylates and down-regulates the motor, a conserved head and neck, and a class-III-specific tail that binds actin and is required for tip targeting.
The allele class matters for what follows. A computational study of kinase-domain variants proposes that abolishing kinase activity and autophosphorylation produces the congenital profound phenotype, while partial or complete inactivation of the protein produces the late-onset progressive one. That is a structural-modelling proposal rather than an established rule, and the largest patient series looked for a genotype-phenotype correlation and did not observe one.

nodes.description: Hair cells with abnormal bundles are not lost at birth; they are lost with age. In the knock-in mouse carrying the equivalent of the human nonsense allele, outer hair cells degenerate with age in a pattern that matches the progression of the hearing loss, and in the kinase-domain knock-in, degeneration is present at six months and more severe at twelve. This age-dependent cellular attrition is what makes DFNB30 a progressive rather than a static hearing loss.
